reviewed_items.summary: Transaction loop has proper error handling with immediate return on failure
proof_trace: core/state_processor.go:109 - for loop iterates over block.Transactions()
core/state_processor.go:110-112 - TransactionToMessage error causes immediate return with wrapped error
core/state_processor.go:116-118 - ApplyTransactionWithEVM error causes immediate return with wrapped error
core/state_processor.go:120-121 - Only on success are receipts/logs appended

counterexample_evaluation.original_concern: Transaction loop continuation logic could benefit from explicit documentation about error handling semantics
counterexample_evaluation.analysis: The code does NOT silently continue on errors. Both TransactionToMessage (line 111) and ApplyTransactionWithEVM (line 117) errors result in immediate function return. The error messages are properly wrapped with transaction index and hash for debugging. This is the correct and intended behavior for block processing - any transaction failure invalidates the entire block.

guards_present: Error check after TransactionToMessage at line 111 with return
Error check after ApplyTransactionWithEVM at line 117 with return
guard_analysis.effectiveness: Complete - all error paths terminate block processing
guard_analysis.bypass_potential: None - Go's error return pattern ensures no bypass

reviewed_items.rationale: The original audit item suggests documentation improvement for error handling semantics. However, the code itself is correct and follows standard Go error handling patterns. The error messages include transaction index and hash which provides sufficient context. This is a false positive as there is no security issue or correctness bug.

reviewed_items.summary: Nonce increment before execution is correct per Ethereum Yellow Paper semantics
proof_trace: core/state_transition.go:509 - SetNonce increments nonce BEFORE call execution
core/state_transition.go:529 - EVM.Call may return vmerr but this doesn't affect nonce
core/state_transition.go:574-578 - ExecutionResult.Err contains vmerr for caller inspection
core/state_transition.go:503 - Comment explains vmerr does not affect consensus

counterexample_evaluation.original_concern: Nonce increment logic is correct but lacks explicit documentation about its persistence across execution failures
counterexample_evaluation.plausibility: None - behavior is correct per specification
counterexample_evaluation.analysis: The nonce MUST be incremented before execution per Ethereum semantics. Even if the transaction execution fails (ErrOutOfGas, ErrExecutionReverted, etc.), the nonce increment persists. This is intentional: it prevents replay attacks and ensures nonces are consumed regardless of execution outcome. The distinction between consensus errors (which prevent transaction inclusion) and VM errors (which still consume the nonce) is fundamental to Ethereum.

guards_present: Nonce validation in preCheck at lines 316-328
Nonce overflow check at lines 325-327 returning ErrNonceMax
guard_analysis.effectiveness: Complete - nonce checked before increment, overflow prevented
guard_analysis.bypass_potential: None - preCheck runs before nonce modification

reviewed_items.rationale: The nonce handling follows Ethereum Yellow Paper specifications exactly. Line 503's comment explicitly states 'vmerr errors do not effect consensus'. The behavior is correct: consensus errors reject the transaction entirely (nonce unchanged), while VM errors allow the transaction but record failure in receipt. Adding documentation might help newcomers but there is no security issue.

reviewed_items.summary: Silent authorization error handling is mandated by EIP-7702 specification
proof_trace: core/state_transition.go:512-517 - Authorization loop processes all authorizations
core/state_transition.go:514 - Comment explicitly states errors are intentionally ignored
core/state_transition.go:515 - applyAuthorization called, errors discarded
core/state_transition.go:583-611 - validateAuthorization returns specific error types
core/state_transition.go:614-638 - applyAuthorization validates then applies delegation

counterexample_evaluation.original_concern: EIP-7702 authorization errors are silently ignored in loop without logging
counterexample_evaluation.analysis: Per EIP-7702 specification, invalid authorizations MUST be skipped silently. The spec states: 'If the authorization is invalid, skip it and continue with the next.' This prevents a single malformed authorization from invalidating an entire batch. The validateAuthorization function (lines 583-611) performs comprehensive checks including chain ID, nonce overflow, signature validity, and code checks. Invalid authorizations simply don't take effect - they don't cause transaction failure.

guards_present: Signature recovery and validation at lines 593-596
Authority added to access list at line 602 even on failure (gas accounting)
guard_analysis.effectiveness: Complete - all invalid authorizations are rejected
guard_analysis.bypass_potential: None - validation is comprehensive per EIP-7702

reviewed_items.rationale: The silent error handling is not a bug but a deliberate design choice mandated by EIP-7702. The comment at line 514 documents this explicitly: 'Note errors are ignored, we simply skip invalid authorizations here.' Each individual authorization is validated independently. Failed authorizations don't affect valid ones in the same batch. This is the correct implementation.

reviewed_items.summary: Jump table lookup is safe - all 256 opcode slots are guaranteed non-nil
proof_trace: core/vm/interpreter.go:188 - operation := jumpTable[op] performs lookup
core/vm/interpreter.go:120 - jumpTable set to evm.table
core/vm/interpreter.go:167 - _ = jumpTable[0] ensures nil-check outside hot loop
core/vm/jump_table.go:69 - JumpTable is [256]*operation fixed-size array
core/vm/jump_table.go:71-87 - validate() panics if any slot is nil
core/vm/jump_table.go:1086-1091 - newFrontierInstructionSet fills all nil slots with opUndefined
core/vm/jump_table.go:1089 - undefined flag set true for unassigned opcodes
core/vm/evm.go:151-182 - Table selection based on chain rules, all paths set valid table

counterexample_evaluation.original_concern: Jump table lookup for undefined opcodes requires verification of all fork-specific tables
counterexample_evaluation.plausibility: None - architectural guarantee prevents nil entries
counterexample_evaluation.analysis: The JumpTable type is a fixed [256]*operation array. The base newFrontierInstructionSet() function explicitly fills ALL 256 slots - lines 1086-1091 iterate over the entire table and set nil entries to opUndefined. Each fork-specific table builds on this base and adds/modifies opcodes. The validate() function (lines 71-87) panics at startup if any slot is nil, providing a compile-time-adjacent guarantee. The EVM initialization in evm.go:151-182 uses a complete switch statement covering all forks, defaulting to frontierInstructionSet.

guards_present: validate() function panics on nil slots at table construction
newFrontierInstructionSet fills all 256 slots before validate
Each fork table inherits from validated parent and re-validates
opUndefined returns ErrInvalidOpCode for undefined opcodes
guard_analysis.bypass_potential: None - would require bypassing Go's array bounds and startup validation

fork_table_verification.frontier: Base table, fills all 256 slots, validated
fork_table_verification.tangerineWhistle: Inherits homestead, modifies gas costs, validated

reviewed_items.rationale: This was flagged as High severity needing verification. After thorough analysis, the code is provably safe. The architectural design ensures no nil pointer dereference is possible: (1) fixed-size array prevents index OOB, (2) base table fills all 256 slots, (3) validate() panics on nil at startup, (4) each fork inherits and re-validates. Undefined opcodes correctly return ErrInvalidOpCode via opUndefined.

summary.notes: All 4 audit items were reviewed. The highest-severity item (EVM jump table lookup) was verified safe through architectural analysis showing multiple layers of nil-protection. The EIP-7702 silent error handling is correct per specification. Nonce handling follows Ethereum Yellow Paper. Transaction loop error handling is properly implemented.
